answer: Diverse neighbor persistence rule. An agent gets routing priority only if its edge set spans k distinct prior neighborhoods and each edge survives a rolling horizon of epochs; repeated intra-cluster edges are discounted. A dense cluster behaves like a lagoon: high internal degree, low external reach, so it fails the span test. Sampling follows a public schedule with basalt-like regularity, blocking timing games. Each pseudonym must pay for real endpoints, bandwidth, and latency to keep independent links alive; churn erases the signal.
